children: Super Micro Computer shares jumped more than 10% in after-hours trading Tuesday after the AI-server maker said preliminary quarterly revenue would significantly exceed its previous forecast. But the good news delivered only a modest lift to chip stocks, which are still struggling to recover from a bruising selloff.
Super Micro assembles servers and data-center systems around chips from suppliers including Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices.

On Tuesday, the company said it expects revenue of $18.5 billion to $19.5 billion for its fiscal first quarter ended Sept. 30, up from the previous forecast of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion. At the midpoint, the new estimate is roughly 27% higher than the old one.

If that forecast holds, revenue would nearly quadruple from a year ago — a striking increase even by the standards of the AI infrastructure boom. The company also raised its estimated gross-profit margin to 12% to 12.5%, up from a previous range of 10.4% to 10.8%.

Shares of Super Micro rose nearly 13% in late trading after closing at $32.47. The enthusiasm spilled over to fellow server makers Dell Technologies and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, which gained 5.3% and 4.5% in after-hours trading, respectively.

The upbeat forecast also provided some relief for chipmakers battered by a recent selloff. Shares in Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, Micron Technology and Marvell Technology all gained roughly 2% in after-hours trading.

Still, the gains represent only a modest recovery after a steep decline in semiconductor shares. Investors aren't necessarily doubting that companies are buying the hardware. They are questioning whether the businesses paying for sprawling data centers can generate enough returns to justify the cost.

Chip shares have been under pressure in recent weeks as higher inflation and borrowing costs have complicated the economics of AI infrastructure. Concerns over debt-laden AI cloud providers, including CoreWeave, have added to the unease.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index suffered an eight-session losing streak before bouncing back Monday. The index was down 0.3% during Tuesday's session, reversing Monday's 1.6% advance.

Super Micro's update offers some reassurance that the buildout hasn't stopped. Stronger-than-expected sales suggest its customers are still buying costly equipment and investing heavily in AI infrastructure. But this doesn't necessarily suggest there is an equivalent increase in industrywide semiconductor demand.
The server maker could be winning business from competitors, selling more expensive systems, or delivering equipment containing chips purchased in previous quarters.
Super Micro's stronger sales don't address the root concern weighing on chip stocks: whether their customers can generate enough returns on their AI investments to keep the spending going.
Super Micro will announce its fiscal first-quarter results on Nov. 3.
